question_text: What is meant by mechanical equilibrium of a rigid body? State its conditions and explain what a couple is.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.why: Equilibrium is a statement about BOTH motions a rigid body can have — along a line and about an axis.
common_mistakes: Defining equilibrium as "at rest". A body moving uniformly is also in equilibrium.

recall.must_convey: That equilibrium means neither linear nor angular momentum changes.
accept: no acceleration and no angular acceleration

steps.label: The two conditions
steps.why: Each condition kills one kind of acceleration; a body needs both to be fully in equilibrium.
common_mistakes: Giving only ΣF = 0 — a couple defeats that single condition.

recall.must_convey: That both the net force and the net torque must vanish.
accept: sigma F zero and sigma tau zero
reject: two equal and opposite separated forces

steps.label: The couple
lines: A couple is a pair of equal and
opposite forces with separated lines of
action. Its net force is zero but its
steps.why: The couple is the standard counter-example that shows why the second condition exists at all.
common_mistakes: Saying a couple is in equilibrium because its forces cancel — its torques do not.

recall.must_convey: That a couple has zero net force but non-zero torque, producing pure rotation.
accept: zero net force non zero torque
reject: sigma F zero and sigma tau zero
